title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: handle waiting conversations when a queue closes or has no representatives signed in
summary: Hold: the briefing describes existing queue overflow rules as running only before queue entry, but Microsoft also documents legacy rules for conversations already waiting. Narrow that comparison to the out-of-operating-hours condition; the roadmap facts, publishing-based credit consumption and administrator opt-in are supported.

claims.where: What's changing: existing overflow rules; Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: The queue's existing overflow rules are evaluated once before queue entry and do not cover conversations already waiting.
claims.quote: A queue's overflow handling options can trigger actions either before or after a work item is queued.
claims.fix: In What's changing replace the comparison with: "Learn says the queue's out-of-operating-hours overflow condition is evaluated once before queue entry, whereas the playbook condition is evaluated continuously, including after transfers." In Governance controls replace the final sentence with: "The queue's out-of-operating-hours condition is evaluated once before queue entry, so it does not respond when the queue closes while conversations are already waiting." This narrows both statements to the condition discussed in https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/manage-overflow#use-natural-language-playbooks-to-configure-overflow-actions-for-work-items-in-queue, without denying the documented legacy wait-time overflow rules.

claims.claim: The playbook out-of-operating-hours condition is evaluated continuously, including after transfers.
claims.quote: the system evaluates the queue overflow rules once only before the system adds the work item to the queue, whereas the playbook condition is evaluated continuously, including after transfers.

claims.claim: The playbook can trigger immediately rather than waiting for time or volume-based conditions.
claims.quote: Configure overflow handling to trigger immediately when eligible service representatives aren't available for a work item or queues are out of operating hours, instead of waiting for time or volume-based conditions.

claims.claim: Without configured overflow handling, a work item enters the queue and the customer waits for a representative.
claims.quote: If you don't set up overflow handling, then by default, the work item is added to the queue and the customer waits to be connected to a service representative.
